items.title: Amazon Aurora MySQL 8.4.10 is now generally available
items.content_snippet: Starting today, Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition 8.4 supports MySQL 8.4.10. We recommend upgrading to the newer minor versions to accept fixes for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in prior versions of MySQL and to benefit from bug fixes, performance improvements, and new functionality added by the MySQL community. items.title: AWS Lambda now supports queues for Apache Kafka in self-managed Kafka event sources
items.content_snippet: AWS Lambda now supports queues for Apache Kafka in self-managed Kafka event source mappings (ESM), for Kafka clusters that customers run themselves and for managed offerings such as Confluent Cloud. Customers can now scale processing for Kafka workloads beyond the partition count of a topic, increasing throughput during traffic spikes and improving processing resilience. items.title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools in flows
items.content_snippet: Amazon Connect Customer now enables you to invoke Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools in customer experience flows through the new 'External Tool' block. With this launch, you can connect flows to third-party applications through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and reuse the same tools used by your agentic experiences to retrieve data or trigger actions, without writing custom Lambda functions. items.title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports Cases and External Tool events in the Wait block
items.content_snippet: Amazon Connect Customer now supports Cases and External Tool events in the Wait block, giving you more control over how your customer experience flows react to real-time data changes. items.title: Make Your AI Agents Predictable With Graph Engineering - Zachary Blumenfeld, Neo4j
items.content_snippet: Graph engineering is a new name for an old idea: give agents a map of the logic they should follow, not just a pile of text. items.title: Your AI Agents Shouldn't Care Where They Run - Nikhil Harithas, Factory
items.content_snippet: Agents can't keep borrowing your identity and running on someone else's machines, especially at banks and other heavily regulated companies. Nikhil Harithas of Factory shows how they rebuilt their coding agent, Droid, to run on any compute inside a customer's own cloud. items.title: Better Search Took This AI Agent From 36% to 98% Accuracy - Aamir Shakir, Mixedbread
items.content_snippet: Agents are smart enough. Most of the time, the real problem is getting them to the right data. Aamir Shakir of Mixedbread explains why the usual stack of OCR, chunking, embeddings and a vector database loses information and leaves agents reading every document. items.title: You Can't Tell What's Real Anymore. Here's What Comes Next - Cristóbal Valenzuela, Runway
items.content_snippet: Runway's first AI film in 2019 was 128x128 pixels. Today, people can't tell generated video from real footage. Runway co-founder and CEO Cristóbal Valenzuela explains how next-frame prediction at scale teaches models physics, object permanence and how the world works. He then shows what happens when those models become real-time and interactive: world interface models, robotics, and Continuum, an early research prototype where anything on your screen can become a live, interactive video. 0:00 In

items.title: Your Company Should Train Its Own AI Models - Will Brown, Prime Intellect
items.content_snippet: Agents relearn the same things every session because the knowledge that runs a company never gets written down. Will Brown of Prime Intellect makes the case for training models on your own traces, feedback and workflows, so they learn on the job the way human coworkers do. He covers evals as test cases, decision models and routing, and widget-style interfaces that turn your decisions into training data. He ends with nightly training runs and an example model trained for about $300K. 0:00 Intro 1
